issues.description: The solution's set_pixel implementation performs an xchg eax, ebx and includes a comment 'Swap registers to match wrong spec', which indicates the solution expects x and y in the opposite registers than the problem statement and the template. The problem statement and template specify x in EAX and y in EBX on entry to set_pixel, but the solution swaps them internally. This mismatch between the documented calling convention and the solution implementation is structural and will confuse students about which registers hold x and y when implementing set_pixel.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the calling convention consistent across all artifacts. Either: (a) update the solution implementation to use x in EAX and y in EBX without performing xchg (and remove the misleading comment), or (b) clearly state in the problem statement and template that the coordinates are passed with x in EBX and y in EAX if that was intended. Ensure the set_pixel implementation and the main caller agree on the register usage.
